QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_40

question.text: A fund's return distribution shows kurtosis of 5.03. This is BEST described as:

answer.text: Leptokurtic — fatter tails and higher peak than normal, indicating elevated outlier risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Kurtosis above 3 (excess kurtosis above zero) is leptokurtic, with fatter tails, a higher peak and elevated outlier risk. A reading of 5.03 indicates elevated tail risk. The Trap: Option C describes platykurtic (kurtosis below 3). Option B describes a mesokurtic / normal distribution (kurtosis = 3). Option D is not a valid statistical interpretation of a 5.03 kurtosis reading. Note: The leptokurtic interpretation is taken from the risk-measure section of the workbook.
